chunks: Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā narrated from al-Ḥusayn ibn Mūsā al-Khashshāb, from Ghiyāth ibn Kallūb, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, from Jaʿfar, from his father, that ʿAlī عليه السلام used to say:
If a chicken, or something similar to it, dies in the well, two or three buckets are drawn from it. But if it is a sheep, or something resembling it, then nine or ten are drawn.

key_terms.الدَّجَاجَةُ: a chicken; a smaller bird whose death in the well entails a lesser amount of water to be drawn
key_terms.الْبِئْرِ: the well from which water is taken and which is being purified
key_terms.شَاةً: a sheep; a larger animal requiring more water to be drawn
key_terms.يُنْزَحُ: water is drawn out; the prescribed act of removing water from the well

ai.seo_question: How much water should be drawn from a well if a dead animal falls into it?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on purifying well water when an animal dies in it. It specifies different amounts of water to be drawn depending on the size of the dead animal, reflecting practical rulings of ritual purity in Shia fiqh.
